host.name: Flor

culture.title: Voseo is the default
culture.note: Porteños say vos, not tú: vos sos, vos tenés, decime, mirá, contame. Using tú sounds foreign; using usted on a date sounds cold.

culture.title: Che
culture.note: A friendly 'hey' that also fills pauses: «Che, ¿y vos qué hacés?». Argentines use it so much that Che Guevara got his nickname from it.

culture.title: Re = very
culture.note: «Re lindo», «re copado», «está re bueno»: re is the everyday intensifier, much more natural than muy on a date.

culture.title: Medialunas and the merienda
culture.note: Late afternoon is merienda time: café con leche or mate with medialunas. Suggesting to share medialunas is a warm, very local move.

culture.title: Mate is shared
culture.note: If someone offers you mate, you drink it all and give it back to the person who serves (el cebador). Saying «gracias» means you don't want more.

nonverbal.norms: Porteños are expressive and direct: steady eye contact, animated faces and leaning in are normal; drifting eyes while someone talks reads as disinterest quickly.

fillers.tip: When you need a second to think, say «este…» or «o sea…» instead of «um».

tips.formal: With someone your age, «vos» feels warmer than «usted».
tips.other: Porteños say «vos sos» and «tenés», not «tú eres» and «tienes».
tips.mixed: You switched between «vos» and «usted»; on a date, stay with «vos».

cultural_moments.milestone: Mate moment: take the mate like a porteño, or match their banter
cultural_moments.evidence: The learner, in Spanish, answers the date's offer of mate: accepts or declines it, says how they take it, or asks about the ritual with curiosity.
cultural_moments.cue: Pull a mate and a thermos out of your bag and offer them some, the way you would with a new friend. One short line.
